findings.issue: 34:1 reads וַיְגָרֲשֵׁהוּ and 34:2 reads אֲבָרֲכָה. Both reshes carry hataf-patah, as the human answered. 34:2 keeps the divineName יְהוָה with no holam, as previously settled.

90:1 reads לָּנוּ (lamed with dagesh). 90:10 reads בָּהֶם (bet with dagesh). 90:16 reads פָּעֳלֶךָ (pe with dagesh, ayin with hataf-qamats). All three match the human answers. The settled readings around them are unchanged: plene שְׁמוֹנִים, no maqaf in יְמֵי שְׁנוֹתֵינוּ or כִּי גָז, and חִישׁ.

34:19 reads יוֹשִֽׁיעַ, with the meteg on the shin beside its hiriq and no mark on the following consonantal yod. I could not dump codepoints with a read-only tool. The machine proof in /tmp/psalms-s66/human-codepoints.json records the order shin, hiriq, meteg, shin-dot and no meteg on the yod. That order is also the canonical (NFC) order. No other meteg was added anywhere, which keeps the settled no-extra-meteg rule.

verdict: Approved for this installment. The human answers are applied exactly: hataf-patah under both reshes; pe with dagesh and ayin with hataf-qamats in פָּעֳלֶךָ; dagesh in בָּהֶם and לָּנוּ; and the meteg on the shin of יוֹשִֽׁיעַ, not on the following yod. The 91:16 repeat is a Hebrew-only structural occurrence that transcludes the single canonical 91:16, so the Hebrew is recited twice and the English once, with no duplicate canonical identity. The user explicitly authorized this reuse. Verse and chapter scopes are bounded, citations are standOff notes, the page breaks inside EN 34:18 and inside 91:2 in both languages are correct, Hebrew 34 is set in verse lines, and the order 19→34→90→91→repeat sits inside the morning scope. No settled question was reopened, and nothing was decided from standard Hebrew. Whole-volume acceptance remains false. The unrelated German glyph in source 57 remains explicitly uncertain.
